newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian president still leads pack in polls.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian president still leads pack in polls.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso remains on top of the polls despite a series of controversies and growing fears over unemployment, an opinion survey published on Thursday showed.
The survey by the Ibope polling institute, published in the Correio Braziliense newspaper, gave Cardoso 32 percent of the vote if elections were held today.
His closest rival, likely leftist Workers Party candidate Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, would get 16 percent of the ballot with former President Jose Sarney trailing at 9.0 percent.
But the survey also showed a high degree of discontent.
A full 44 percent of those questioned did not think Brazil was heading in the right direction while 42 percent did.
Sixty-two percent said unemployment was their main concern, while 39 percent were worried about the state of health services and 27 percent cited drugs as the main problem facing Brazil.
Ibope, which carried out the survey on behalf of the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), interviewed 3,000 people across Brazil three weeks ago. No margin of error was given.
The poll was carried out following a series of controversies.

Two months ago, the governors of Acre and Amazonas states were accused of paying deputies $190,000 each to vote in favour of a bill that would allow Cardoso and other executive officers to seek re-election.
And a Senate inquiry was expected to conclude next week a six-month-long probe of allegedly fraudulent debt issues by states and municipalities.
